promptText: Some argue governments should ban private cars in city centres to reduce pollution. Others believe individuals should have the right to drive wherever they wish. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

promptText: Some argue that competitive sport teaches children discipline and resilience. Others believe competition breeds needless stress and that youth sport should simply be fun. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

The comparative merits of team sports and individual athletic pursuits.
The decline of physical activity among children in the developed world.

The physical fitness that regular athletic training confers upon growing children.
The identification of exceptional talent at the earliest possible age.

rewarding the most gifted competitors with places in representative teams
instilling obedience to the coach through the discipline of daily training routines

The erosion of unstructured play as organised fixtures colonise the leisure of the young.

distractors: Professional footballers released by their clubs in the closing years of their careers.

phases.correct: the distress is traceable to adult conduct and selection design rather than to competition itself

distractors: every school should abolish competitive fixtures entirely so that no child is ever ranked against another

promptText: Some believe advertising aimed at children should be banned outright. Others argue it teaches them about the marketplace and how to make choices. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

promptText: Some think it is acceptable for minority languages to disappear if it makes global communication easier. Others believe governments should spend money to keep them alive. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

promptText: Some think the government should bear the full cost of housing and caring for the elderly. Others believe families should take sole responsibility for their older relatives. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
